preamble: Hlonipha (avoidance-speech) substitution: Zulu and Xhosa xola, with a lateral click [ǁ], is described as an avoidance term formed from phola 'cool down, be calm' (< Proto-Bantu *-póda). The initial aspirated [pʰ] is replaced by a click and the rest of the word stays the same. In Zulu xola means 'be peaceful, calm'; in Xhosa it means 'forgive'. Herbert (1990) and others argued that hlonipha (avoidance by married women of sounds in in-laws' names) helped clicks spread into Nguni vocabulary (cited in Sands & Gunnink 2019); Gunnink (2023) argues that hlonipha alone cannot account for it, pointing also to identity marking and sound symbolism. This is lexical replacement, not regular sound change. Only one example is attested, so certainty is 2.
phoneticEffects: Click Insertion, Hlonipha Substitution, Lexical Replacement
